questions.stem: 'To burn the midnight oil' means —
options: To study or work late into the night
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to working or studying far into the night, from the era of oil lamps.

questions.stem: 'A white elephant' means —
questions.explanation: It denotes something expensive to maintain but of no real use.

questions.stem: 'To let the cat out of the bag' means —
questions.explanation: The idiom means to disclose a secret, usually by accident.

questions.stem: 'To turn a deaf ear' means —
questions.explanation: It means to deliberately ignore what someone says.

questions.stem: 'A red letter day' means —
questions.explanation: Important days were once marked in red on calendars, hence a specially memorable day.

questions.stem: 'In black and white' means —
questions.explanation: 'In black and white' means recorded in written form.

questions.stem: 'Once in a blue moon' means —
questions.explanation: It describes something that happens very infrequently.

questions.stem: 'To put up with' means —
questions.explanation: 'Put up with' means to endure or tolerate something unpleasant.

questions.stem: It is high time we ___ our habits.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by the past tense even though it refers to the present.

questions.stem: He as well as his brothers ___ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: With 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject, which is singular here.

questions.stem: The number of students in the class ___ increasing.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' takes a plural one.

questions.stem: I would rather ___ than beg.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive without 'to'.

questions.stem: If I were you, I ___ the offer.
questions.explanation: The second conditional pairs 'if + were' with 'would + base verb'.

questions.stem: Neither he nor I ___ responsible for it.
questions.explanation: With 'neither…nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is 'I'.

questions.stem: He does not like ___ in the rain.
questions.explanation: 'Like' is commonly followed by a gerund when speaking of an activity in general.

questions.stem: In 'Honesty is the best policy', the word 'honesty' is a —
questions.explanation: A quality that cannot be perceived by the senses is an abstract noun.

questions.stem: In 'He runs very fast', the word 'very' is a —
questions.explanation: 'Very' modifies the adverb 'fast', so it is itself an adverb of degree.

questions.stem: In 'The crowd was large', the word 'crowd' is a —
questions.explanation: A word naming a group taken as one unit is a collective noun.

questions.stem: In 'Alas! He is dead', the word 'Alas' is a —
questions.explanation: A word expressing sudden emotion is an interjection.

questions.stem: In 'He sat under the tree', the word 'under' is a —
questions.explanation: It shows the relation between 'sat' and 'the tree', so it is a preposition.

questions.stem: In 'She is a beautiful singer', the word 'beautiful' is a —
questions.explanation: It qualifies the noun 'singer', so it is an adjective.

questions.stem: In 'Rahim and Karim are friends', the word 'and' is a —
questions.explanation: A word joining two words or clauses is a conjunction.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is one of the best boy who has come.
He is one of the best boys who has come.
He is one of the best boys who have come.
He is one of best boys who have come.
questions.explanation: In 'one of the + plural noun + who', the relative clause verb agrees with the plural noun.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Accommodation' takes a double c and a double m.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Committee' has a double m, a double t and a double e.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Separate' is spelt with an 'a' in the middle — a very common error.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: Each of the boys have a pen.
Each of the boys has a pen.
Each of the boy has a pen.
Each of the boy have a pen.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a plural noun but a singular verb.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: The rule 'i before e except after c' gives 'receive'.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'benevolent'.
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous'.
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'alleviate'.
questions.explanation: 'Alleviate' means to make suffering or a problem less severe.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'frugal'.
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means sparing with money, so its opposite is 'extravagant'.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'transparent'.
questions.explanation: 'Transparent' lets light through; 'opaque' does not.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'ancient'.
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means belonging to the distant past; its opposite is 'modern'.
